title: Serbian / Montenegrin — ICAO Doc 9303 MRZ (Gaj's Latin without diacritics)
authority: ICAO Doc 9303 Part 3 (8th ed., 2021) §6.A applied to Gaj's Latin; Montenegro, Pravilnik o sadržaju mašinski čitljivog zapisa (2008), Art. 5(4)
description: Machine-readable-zone style ASCII for Serbian and Montenegrin names: write in Gaj's Latin, then drop diacritics per ICAO §6.A (Đ→D, Ć/Č→C, Š→S, Ž→Z, Dž→DZ, Lj/Nj kept). Ђоковић → Dokovic.
notes: Open question: Đ→D or DJ in Serbian MRZs. No Serbian primary source was found. ICAO §6.A gives Đ→D; Montenegro's 2008 MRZ regulation, Art. 5(4), says 'Đ kao D, Ž kao Z, Ć kao C, Č kao C i Š kao S'; a BiH 2002 ID-card rulebook reportedly says the same (unverified); Serbian ID-card MRZs strip diacritics. D is used here; generate DJ (sr_ascii) too when matching.
ICAO §6.B lists Serbian Г as H. This is an error copied from the Belarusian/Ukrainian rule and is NOT applied: Г→G (Гордана → Gordana).

ICAO §6.B row '0402' is printed with the Ћ glyph and Ћ (U+040B) itself is missing; this scheme follows Gaj's Latin (Ђ→Đ→D, Ћ→Ć→C). The other ICAO Serbian exceptions (Ж→Z, Ч→C, Ш→S, Х→H, Ц→C, Џ→DZ) agree.
The visual zone of Serbian passports uses Gaj's Latin with diacritics (sr_gaj). Case is restored from the source; upper-casing and MRZ punctuation/filler rules belong to the MRZ formatter.
Montenegrin С́/З́ → S/Z (ICAO Ś→S, Ź→Z); combining stress marks are dropped.
